items.headline: SIA steward collapses with a faint pulse on a Chengdu flight, saved by a doctor on board
items.summary: A Singapore Airlines cabin-crew member on a flight from Chengdu to Singapore collapsed mid-air with a faint pulse and cold limbs. A former medical professional among the passengers stepped in and cared for him for the rest of the journey.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines and Scoot put over 380,000 discounted tickets on sale
items.summary: SIA and Scoot are running a 'Time To Fly' promotion with more than 380,000 discounted return tickets on sale from Oct 23 to 30, 2026, spanning routes across both carriers' networks.

items.headline: Man, 44, jailed 80 days for shoving a seven-year-old boy twice at an indoor playground
items.summary: A Singaporean man was sentenced to 80 days' jail after pleading guilty to voluntarily causing hurt to a child under 14. He had shoved the boy twice at an indoor playground after the child hit his daughter.

items.headline: Update: Singapore parents jailed over their eight-month-old son's abuse death
items.summary: A couple were sentenced for the abuse and death of their eight-month-old son, who was shaken and smothered. The 23-year-old mother was jailed 15 years and 3 months and the 27-year-old father 16 years, after pleading guilty earlier in October.

items.headline: Modi accuses Rahul Gandhi of risking 'disorder' and tarnishing India's image
items.summary: At the NDTV World Summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi hit out at opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party, accusing them of seeking to tarnish India's reputation amid the continuing voter-roll protests.

items.headline: India's youth-led 'Cockroach' protest movement hardens into Modi's main opposition
items.summary: Bloomberg reports that the student and youth protests over alleged voter-roll manipulation, nicknamed the 'Cockroach' movement, have become the most organised challenge to Modi's government, demanding the chief election commissioner resign.

items.headline: The rupee slides toward a record 100-per-dollar as foreign investors pull out
items.summary: Strategists expect the rupee to keep weakening toward the 100-per-dollar mark into 2027, pressured by record foreign-investor outflows, high oil prices and a widening import bill, even as the RBI intervenes to steady the currency.

items.headline: Royal London bets on long-dated gilts before Burnham's first Budget
items.summary: Royal London Asset Management said it has turned overweight on 30-year UK government bonds, wagering that Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey will rein in the deficit at the Oct 28 Budget, even as Britain carries the G7's highest borrowing costs.

items.headline: Melania Trump brokers a narrow humanitarian ceasefire in occupied Oleshky
items.summary: The White House said US First Lady Melania Trump helped secure a localised ceasefire in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city in Kherson, to let aid in and civilians out. Al Jazeera and Russian and Ukrainian officials cited an Oct 27 start; the White House gave Oct 29.

items.headline: Update: Israel raids West Bank towns and uproots 2,000 in Hebron before the election
items.summary: Israeli forces raided at least 15 towns across the northern occupied West Bank and forced some 2,000 people from their homes in Hebron, part of a widening operation as Israel prepares to close West Bank crossings for Tuesday's general election.

items.headline: Sudan's shift to drone warfare deepens its civilian catastrophe
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports that Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces are leaning ever more on drones, driving up civilian casualties far from the front lines, as a UN-backed monitor warns of spreading famine risk across Darfur and Kordofan.

items.headline: Anthropic lines up a mid-November IPO, Wall Street's biggest AI listing yet
items.summary: Anthropic is pressing ahead with a potential mid-November public listing, with its investor roadshow expected the week of Nov 9, according to Bloomberg. Investors reportedly see a fair value of US$1.8 trillion to US$2 trillion, roughly double its May funding round.

items.headline: Update: OpenAI's roughly US$30 billion private round is led by Coatue and UAE investors
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI's new raise of up to US$30 billion, at a US$1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, is being led by Coatue and investors in the UAE, serving as a bridge ahead of a possible later IPO. Terms are still being negotiated.

items.headline: Markets expect the Fed to hold rates at its Oct 28 meeting, with December in play
items.summary: Traders are overwhelmingly betting the Federal Reserve will leave rates at 3.75%-4.00% when it decides on Oct 28, even as inflation stays sticky. Attention has shifted to a possible December hike and to how Chair Kevin Warsh frames the path at his press conference.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli wins the US Grand Prix from pole but is denied an early title
items.summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli converted pole position into victory at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin. George Russell and Lewis Hamilton finished high enough to keep the championship mathematically alive, so his title celebrations are on hold.

items.headline: 🏎️ The Formula 1 title race heads to Mexico as Antonelli's crown is delayed
items.summary: Antonelli leads the drivers' standings on 340 points, well clear of team-mate Russell and Ferrari's Hamilton, but his bid to seal the championship in Austin fell short. The title will now be decided at the next round in Mexico.

items.headline: 🏏 India lead New Zealand 2-0 heading into the third T20I in Wellington
items.summary: India go into the third T20I at Wellington on Oct 27 leading the five-match series 2-0 after back-to-back wins in Christchurch. New Zealand, who must win to stay alive, have reshuffled their squad, with Lockie Ferguson missing the match.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz returns to Vienna as Wawrinka bids an emotional farewell in Basel
items.summary: The ATP 500 double-header is under way. Carlos Alcaraz opens his Vienna campaign against Karen Khachanov while Alexander Zverev eyes the year-end No. 1, and in Basel home favourite Stan Wawrinka retires as Novak Djokovic returns for the first time since 2011.

items.headline: An implant that burns up excess blood sugar with electricity passes mouse tests
items.summary: Scientific American reports on a USB-sized implant from ETH Zurich's Martin Fussenegger that uses an inorganic electrocatalyst to strip glucose from the blood, lowering blood sugar without insulin or living cells. Published in Science, it worked reliably over six weeks in mice.

items.headline: Asteroid Bennu's samples are rewriting how the Solar System formed
items.summary: New isotope analysis of grains returned by NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission suggests Bennu's parent body formed near the water-ice line, inside the orbit of a growing Jupiter. Scientific American reports the findings are reshaping ideas about where the Solar System's building blocks mixed.

items.headline: Japan's MMX mission sets off to sample Mars's moon Phobos
items.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft, carrying the Franco-German Idefix rover, has launched toward Mars to study Phobos and Deimos. It aims to collect a sample from Phobos and return it to Earth around 2031, which would be the first sample from a Martian moon.

fun_fact.headline: The Dead Sea is salty enough to float on
fun_fact.body: The Dead Sea is so salty — about 34% salinity, roughly 10 times saltier than the ocean — that the water is dense enough to make swimmers bob on the surface like a cork, unable to sink. That same punishing saltiness is why almost nothing can live in it, which is how the lake earned its name.

puzzle.title: Overlapping Squares
puzzle.body:
Two identical squares overlap. One square is pinned so that a corner of the second square sits exactly on the first square's centre, and the second square is then free to rotate to any angle about that centre point.

As the top square spins, the size and shape of the overlapping region keep changing. What fraction of a single square's area does the overlap cover — and does the answer depend on the angle?
puzzle.approach: Fix the pinned corner and rotate — think about what the four-fold symmetry does to the regions around the centre.
puzzle.answer:
The overlap is always exactly one quarter (1/4) of a square's area, no matter the rotation angle.

Why: the pinned corner sits at the centre of the lower square, and its two edges meet at a right angle. Those edges split the lower square into four quarters around the centre. As the top square rotates, one of its edges sweeps area out of one quarter while its perpendicular edge sweeps an identical area into the neighbouring quarter. By the four-fold symmetry about the centre the gains and losses cancel exactly, so the covered region is forever one quarter of the square.

word_puzzle.title: Strike Up the Band
word_puzzle.body:
LETTER BOXED — use every one of the 12 letters at least once, in as few words as possible.

Rules: words of 3+ letters; consecutive letters must come from different sides; each word after the first must start with the previous word's last letter.

   Top:    O · J · Y
   Right:  U · E · L
   Bottom: K · B · P
   Left:   X · H · N

There is a clean two-word solution that uses all 12 letters.
word_puzzle.approach: Each new word must begin with the previous word's last letter, and consecutive letters can never share a side — hunt for a first word that ends on a tricky letter.
word_puzzle.answer:
JUKEBOX  then  XYLOPHONE

JUKEBOX runs J-U-K-E-B-O-X, then XYLOPHONE picks up the trailing X and runs X-Y-L-O-P-H-O-N-E. Between them the two words touch all 12 letters, and no step ever uses two letters from the same side.
